_source: Recovered from community Linux tools plus the real Pulsar Fusion Windows installer, then confirmed on hardware. Full provenance: docs/profiles/pulsar-x2h-mini.md

match._note: The mouse enumerates as 3554:f507 whether connected by cable or through the 2.4GHz dongle -- same identity, same hidraw node, no wired/wireless profile split. 25a7:fa7b/fa7c are Cfg.ini's alternate ids with no hardware here to confirm. f509 is the receiver's own identity, kept in case a pairing state exposes it. Do NOT add 3710:1403 (X2H Wired Medium): different, 64-byte register-addressed protocol, needs its own profile.

transport._note: Raw USB Output report (SET_REPORT) at report id 0x08, read back over the interrupt IN endpoint -- not the Feature transport the descriptor's feature-report id 6 first suggested. hskctl's transport.kind "output" implements exactly this shape.

commands._note: 'battery'/'version' are their own opcodes (byte 1), data from byte 2. Everything else is the dongle's memory-mapped get/set (opcode 0x08/0x07 at a fixed address baked into each template): byte 3:4 address (written big-endian), byte 5 length, value from byte 6. Every scalar write carries a valueChecksum byte ('sum8_minus_55' = 0x55 - value) immediately after the value, separate from the whole-packet checksum.

sleep._note: address 0xb7, 'units of 10s'; the field speaks seconds via scale:10.

batteryPercent._note: Reads a plausible, stable percentage across repeated status calls on real hardware.

charging._note: Correctly flips with the cable going in or out, confirmed on hardware.

firmwareVersion._note: Stable major.minor (2.24) across repeated status calls.

ui.label: Polling rate
ui.description: How often the mouse reports its position

pollingRate._note: 1000 <-> 4000 Hz round-tripped exactly on real hardware. 8000 is real in the register map but unconfirmed on this 4K dongle, so it stays out of uiOptions.

dpiStageCount._needsVerification: Writing it had a real destructive side effect: setting 4 reset the whole DPI table to factory defaults. Locked read-only; revisit only with a capture of what Pulsar Fusion actually does.

activeDpiStage._note: Diagnostics only. Wire value is 0-based; add:1 keeps the 1-based convention. Writes round-trip (byte stores and reads back) but never change the mouse's live output, and the physical DPI button does not switch stages either -- which is why this profile is the stage-switcher's refusal half: read-only here, until a capture finds the real mechanism. See _followUp.

ui.label: Lift-off distance
ui.description: How far above the desk the sensor keeps tracking

liftOffDistance._note: Write path confirmed via the motionSync canary; the reading is plausible, not independently cross-checked.

debounceMs._note: Field reads 3 on this mouse; Cfg.ini [DEV_13] Debounce=3 is this model's factory default.

ui.label: Motion sync
ui.description: Align sensor reads to the polling clock

motionSync._note: The canary field: its write path was verified first, alone, before any other scalar write was trusted on this transport.

angleSnap._note: Write path confirmed on hardware via the motionSync canary.

rippleControl._note: Write path confirmed on hardware via the motionSync canary.

ui.label: Turbo mode
ui.description: Report clicks faster than the switch debounces

turboMode._note: Write path confirmed on hardware via the motionSync canary.

sleepSeconds._note: The stored value is units of 10s; scale:10 keeps the field in seconds. Reading 30 matches the owner's observed auto-sleep.

dpiStage1._note: `hskctl set dpiStage1 3200` round-tripped exactly and the cursor speed changed -- confirmed with the real device in hand. Stage 1 only, deliberately: no mechanism was ever found that makes another stage live.

dpiStage1Color._note: Confirmed on real hardware: the LED visibly changed.

_followUp: Stage switching: no mechanism found. activeDpiStage round-trips but never changes live output; the physical DPI button does nothing; dpiStageCount=4 (Cfg.ini's factory default) reset the DPI table and still did not fix switching. The real mechanism is most likely a dedicated command distinct from the plain memory writes nordic.py assumes -- compare CMD_ACTIVE_PROFILE_SET. Needs a live USB capture of Pulsar Fusion switching stages.
1K dongle variant unconfirmed: check the USB ids match (hskctl probe) and whether >1000 Hz actually applies; values/uiOptions may need adjusting, possibly a separate profile.
The RF receiver identity (3554:f509) has never been seen carrying the config protocol; plausibly droppable from match.productIds, kept for lack of positive evidence.
8000 Hz is in `values` (register map confirmed on a Nordic-family sibling) but withheld from `uiOptions` until an 8K dongle exists to test against.

Two low-risk gaps vs the real driver: autosleep mirrors only 0xB7 (the driver also writes 0xAD, ADDR_AUTOSLEEP_ALT), and unsolicited reports can desync a naive read-once -- the driver retries until resp[1] matches the sent opcode, check_ack here only matches a fixed byte.
